subject: Transactional vs batch traffic: sizing probe for EmberPay pilot

Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: EmberPay pilot — traffic profile (initial)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. Per request, attaching a small sample of our production traffic and a short note on transactional vs batch workloads. High level: our checkout service is very spiky (sub-second needs on auth/gateway calls) but about 30% of traffic is behind a batch enrichment pipeline that can tolerate 200–500ms. We know these two shapes will have very different coverage/reliability needs.

Questions we have for sizing:
- How do you suggest we price/reserve capacity across a mixed workload?
- What concurrency per GPU is realistic if we prioritize p50 latency for transactional calls?
- Any thresholds where we should consider separate pools (dedicated for low-latency vs shared for batch)?

Attached: emberpay-traffic-sample.csv (500 rows, token counts + timestamps).

Looking forward — can we hop on a short follow-up tomorrow?

Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
EmberPay

Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay pilot — traffic profile (initial)

Samir — thanks for the sample, this is exactly the kind of data we need. Quick notes and a couple of clarifying asks before the follow-up:

1) Two traffic shapes: good to call these out explicitly ("auth/checkout" = transactional, p50/p95 targets sub-200ms; "enrichment" = batch, p95 okay up to 500ms). That lets us size separate pools or multi-tenant routing rules.

2) Prompt/response lengths: the CSV has a token distribution column but we need a short histogram for 3 buckets: short (<64 tokens), medium (64–512), long (>512). Can you send counts for those?

3) Sessionization and KV cache: are the checkout flows using session affinity (sticky sessions) that would benefit from KV cache warmness, or are requests independent? Sticky sessions change how many concurrent sessions map to active KV entries per pod.

4) Cold-start tolerance: for auth calls, what percent of requests can tolerate an extra 50–100ms at cold start?

I've attached a short intake worksheet (dedicated-sizer-intake.pdf) that lists the fields we typically use to run the sizing. If you prefer, we can run an initial projection and present two options: (A) conservative — isolated low-latency pool + separate batch pool, (B) mixed with QoS routing and on-demand burst.

Proposing a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT — does that work for you and Lexi?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: EmberPay pilot — traffic profile (initial)

Forwarding a few practical heuristics from infra side — Vivek

On our sizing heuristics:
- Transactional (sub-200ms target): assume 4–6 concurrent requests per A100-ish GPU for 16k context LLM at optimized kernels if you maintain KV cache affinity. If requests are stateless, plan for 2–3 concurrent to hit p95.
- Batch (<=500ms): you can push higher multiplexing (10–20 concurrent) depending on prompt length distribution; batching will dramatically help token throughput.
- If short prompts dominate (<64 tokens) and session affinity exists, favor an isolated pool with smaller instance counts (keeps p50/p95 tight).
- For mixed pools, use smart routing: route transactional to reserved fast lane; overflow to mixed pool with a fallback model (smaller/quantized) on capacity pressure.

I'll prepare a quick projection after we get the token histogram and session-affinity answers.

From: Samir Patel <samir@emberpay.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Lexi Ortega <lexi.ops@emberpay.com>, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 15:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: EmberPay pilot — traffic profile (initial)

Aditya / Vivek — thanks for the rapid follow-up. Answers below and a short note inline.

- Token histogram: short=62% (<64), medium=33% (64–512), long=5% (>512). Will upload a 7-day sample to the Drive link you shared.
- Sessionization: checkout uses a sticky session (we use a session cookie that keeps user affinity for ~90s).
- Cold-start tolerance: ~10% of auth calls can tolerate +100ms, but we want cold-starts to be rare.

We prefer option A (isolated low-latency pool + separate batch). Please proceed with a conservative projection and include an estimated monthly cost delta vs the mixed routing approach so execs can compare.

Thanks — meeting confirmed for tomorrow 10am PT.

Samir
